# An R interface to peekbank

The `peekbankr` package allows you to access data in
[Peekbank](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbank-website/), an open
database of developmental eye-tracking data, from R. Data are retrieved
from the versioned [peekbank dataset on
Redivis](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank); the `get_`
functions return tidy tables without you having to write queries. The
package vignette provides examples of the data loading functions and
what the resulting data look like.

### Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("peekbank/peekbankr")
```

The first data request will open a browser window to authorize Redivis
access (free account). For non-interactive use, set a
`REDIVIS_API_TOKEN` environment variable instead. That token needs the
`data.metadata` scope.

### Usage

``` r

library(tidyverse)
library(peekbankr)

pb <- peekbank("2026.1")   # create a peekbank client with a database version

data <- pb$aoi_timepoints %>%
  left_join(pb$administrations)
```

This downloads the datasets automatically for the first access and
caches them for subsequent use.

If you only want to download a subset of the release,
`pb$subset$<table>()` takes `dplyr` expressions and returns only the
matching rows:

``` r

aoi_timepoints <- pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016")
administrations <- pb$subset$administrations(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016")

ps_data <- aoi_timepoints %>%
  left_join(administrations)
```

Predicates are `dplyr` expressions. A predicate can name any column of
the table, or columns of any table that a row of the queried table is
connected to:

``` r

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(age >= 24, age <= 36, sex == "female")
pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(vanilla_trial, !excluded)
pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(target_stimulus_novelty == "familiar")
pb$subset$administrations(sex == "female")
pb$subset$trials(vanilla_trial)
```

These also work across tables:

``` r

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016",
                         age < 24 & vanilla_trial)
```

The exception is **`t_norm`** on `pb$subset$aoi_timepoints()`, as by
default we transfers the table run-length encoded (one row per run of a
constant AOI) and t_norm filters would result in unintuitive behavior.
If you need to filter t_norm, either do it on the fetched result OR pass
`rle = FALSE` to read the expanded table directly (which will make the
fetch take a lot longer):

``` r

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016", t_norm > 0) # Error

pb$subset$aoi_timepoints(dataset_name == "pomper_saffran_2016", t_norm > 0,
                         rle = FALSE)
```

Every other column filters normally, including `aoi`, which is constant
within a run. `pb$subset$xy_timepoints()` is not encoded, so it has no
such restriction.

For the timepoint tables, the predicates are translated to remote SQL
queries, so only a subset of predicates is available. If you use a
predicate that cannot be translated to a query, an error message will
let you know. The smaller tables are filtered in R, so they take
arbitrary `dplyr` expression.

### Server-side queries

`pb$db` holds a [dbplyr](https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/) handle on each
table. `dplyr` verbs on it compile to SQL and run on the server; data
transfer happens when you `collect()`. Here is an example that
summarises a timepoint table without pulling it:

``` r

pb$db$aoi_timepoints %>%
  group_by(aoi) %>%
  count() %>%
  collect()
```

`pb$db` also holds `aoi_timepoints_rle`, one row per run of a constant
AOI, for anyone who wants the stored shape rather than the samples it
expands to.

Print the client to see the release it is pinned to and what is on it:

``` r

pb
#> <peekbank> release 2026.1 (Redivis version v1.4)
#>   tables:  datasets subjects administrations trials trial_types stimuli
#>            aoi_region_sets aoi_timepoints xy_timepoints
#>   methods: clear_cache() images() query() readmes()
#>   subset:  $subset$<table>(<dplyr predicates>)
#>   db:      $db$<table> for a dbplyr handle, read on collect()
```

### Database versions

Peekbank is released in named versions (e.g. `2026.1`), and
[`peekbank()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/peekbank.md)
requires one.
[`get_db_info()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_db_info.md)
lists what is available.

Pass `"current"` to take whichever version was published most recently
for testing, but this is strongly discouraged as future version releases
will make the same code produce different results.

``` r

pb <- peekbank("2026.1")
pb$release   # "2026.1"
```

### Data files

Raw data, processed intermediates, and per-dataset READMEs live in the
companion [peekbank_files
dataset](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank_files):

``` r

readmes <- pb$readmes(datasets = "pomper_saffran_2016")  # dataset documentation
stimuli <- pb$images(datasets = "reflook_v4")             # stimulus images
```

### Development

After making changes, run `roxygen2::roxygenise()` to update exports and
documentation, and
[`testthat::test_local()`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_package.html)
for the offline test suite.

Running the full test suite requires Redivis credentials: Without them
the network tests skip. Copy `.Renviron.template` to `.Renviron`, fill
in a personal API token from your [Redivis
workspace](https://redivis.com/workspace) settings, and set
`PEEKBANK_NETWORK_TESTS=true`.

# Package index

## Reading Peekbank data

Create a client pinned to one release, then read tables from it.

- [`peekbank()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/peekbank.md)
  : Connect to Peekbank
- [`PeekbankClient`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/PeekbankClient.md)
  : Peekbank client
- [`peekbank_releases()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/peekbank_releases.md)
  : Peekbank releases

## Working with the data

Helpers for the shapes Peekbank data arrives in.

- [`unpack_aux_data()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/unpack_aux_data.md)
  : Unpack the json sting in the \*\_aux_data column and turns it into a
  nested R list
- [`cleanup_cdi_data()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/cleanup_cdi_data.md)
  : Checks cdi data for inconsistencies, warns about them, and fixes
  them
- [`populate_cdi_percentiles()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/populate_cdi_percentiles.md)
  : Populate the provided cdi data with percentile values for that
  specific age, instrument_type, measure and language. Loosely based on
  the work from this repo
  https://github.com/kachergis/cdi-percentiles/tree/main by George
  Kachergis and Jess Mankewitz with advice from Virginia Marchman.
- [`append_relative_cdi_scores()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/append_relative_cdi_scores.md)
  : Adds a relative cdi score indicating the percentage of total
  achievable points the subject got on each given measure

## Preparing a dataset for import

Used by the import scripts in peekbank-data-import, not by analyses.

- [`ds.compute_aois()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.compute_aois.md)
  : Classify gaze samples into AOIs based x/y coordinates and provided
  region sets
- [`ds.get_json_fields()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.get_json_fields.md)
  : Fetching the list of field names and requirements in each table
  according to the schema json file
- [`ds.get_peekjson()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.get_peekjson.md)
  : parse the bundled peekbank schema json into a dataframe
- [`ds.is_table_required()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.is_table_required.md)
  : Check if a certain table is required according to schema
- [`ds.list_coding_methods()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.list_coding_methods.md)
  : Get the coding method list from json schema file
- [`ds.list_ds_tables()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.list_ds_tables.md)
  : List the tables required based on coding method
- [`ds.list_language_choices()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.list_language_choices.md)
  : List current allowed language choices for db import
- [`ds.map_columns()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.map_columns.md)
  : Function for mapping raw data columns to processed table columns
- [`ds.normalize_times()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.normalize_times.md)
  : sets the starting point of a given trial to be zero
- [`ds.resample_times()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.resample_times.md)
  : This function resample times to be consistent across labs.
- [`ds.rezero_times()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.rezero_times.md)
  : sets the starting point of a given trial to be zero
- [`ds.validate_for_db_import()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.validate_for_db_import.md)
  : check all csv files against database schema for database import
- [`ds.validate_table()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.validate_table.md)
  : Check if a dataframe/table is compliant to peekbank json before
  database import
- [`ds.validate_trial_uniqueness_constraint()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/ds.validate_trial_uniqueness_constraint.md)
  : Check if within aoi_timepoints table, there is no duplication in all
  the administration_ids associated with each individual trial_id

## Superseded

The interface before the client. These still work and are not going
away, but a client pins one release for a whole analysis, which these
cannot.

- [`connect_to_peekbank()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/connect_to_peekbank.md)
  : Connect to Peekbank
- [`get_db_info()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_db_info.md)
  : Get information on database connection options
- [`list_peekbank_tables()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/list_peekbank_tables.md)
  : List of peekbank tables
- [`get_datasets()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_datasets.md)
  : Get datasets
- [`get_subjects()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_subjects.md)
  : Get subjects
- [`get_administrations()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_administrations.md)
  : Get administrations
- [`get_trials()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_trials.md)
  : Get trials
- [`get_trial_types()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_trial_types.md)
  : Get trial types
- [`get_stimuli()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_stimuli.md)
  : Get stimuli
- [`get_aoi_region_sets()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_aoi_region_sets.md)
  : Get AOI region sets
- [`get_aoi_timepoints()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_aoi_timepoints.md)
  : Get AOI timepoints
- [`get_xy_timepoints()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_xy_timepoints.md)
  : Get XY timepoints
- [`get_sql_query()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_sql_query.md)
  : Run a SQL query against peekbank
- [`download_stimuli()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/download_stimuli.md)
  : Download stimulus images for the Peekbank repository
- [`get_readmes()`](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/reference/get_readmes.md)
  : Download dataset README files
